corroborating-execution_01_transfer_ab_b.note: corroboration only: never pooled with the 60-frame verdict, because runs of a different length are not more samples of the same experiment

verdict.primary_question: Does the reduced order regress end-to-end performance under a counterbalanced protocol?
verdict.primary_rule: the pooled median of the reduced order's kept runs is at least the pooled median of the legacy order's kept runs

required_checks.detail: every pooled and corroborating execution passed both
pooled kept medians point - and the paired median ratio points +

verdict.rule: Warmup pairs are published and excluded: an execution names its kept run ids and only those reach a median, a ratio, a pair or the sign test. The gate asks the non-regression question and nothing stronger - no p-value threshold is applied in either direction - but it does require the instrument to have been built balanced, and it requires the two readings of that instrument, the pooled medians and the paired ratios, to agree about which way they point. If they point opposite ways the honest answer is that the instrument gave a contradiction, which is NOT_READY rather than a choice of the nicer number.
secondary_evidence: exact sign test over kept pairs

sign_test.used_for: secondary evidence only; no threshold in this file reads it

warmup_policy: an execution publishes runs_used_for_medians; only those runs reach a pooled median, a paired ratio or the sign test. The warmup runs are still in this file, with included_in_performance_verdict=false
why_pooled: one execution of the protocol is a median of two runs, and the same order of the same code measures 1.2-52% apart between runs on this machine; that instrument cannot resolve the difference the performance gate is asked about, in either direction
